_comment: Which economy_data.sii attributes the builder scales, and by which multiplier.
Money and XP are scaled independently so you can, for example, run 10x money with 1x XP.
money_fields: the four per-km salary coefficients. Job payout is roughly
revenue_per_km_base * <the coefficient for that job type> * distance * cargo/urgency modifiers,
so scaling the coefficients scales take-home pay for every job type uniformly while leaving
the relative balance between freight market / cargo market / quick jobs / AI drivers intact.
revenue_per_km_base is deliberately NOT scaled: it would compound with the coefficients.
xp_fields: XP awarded per unit of distance (or as a flat bonus, for the parking entries).
exp_fields_never_scale: exp_* attributes that are thresholds/resolutions rather than XP amounts.
Any other exp_* attribute found in a base file is reported but left alone unless --scale-all-exp.
_reference_defaults_comment: Stock values used ONLY by --standalone mode, which has no base file to read from.
They are community-reported reference values and differ between game versions and
between ATS and ETS2. Patch mode (--base) ignores this table entirely and scales
whatever your game actually ships. Prefer patch mode.
